title: Backend: when extremes happened + incremental aggregate refresh
description: Hourly and daily aggregates gain temp_min_at, temp_max_at, wind_gust_max_at, plus humidity and pressure min/max. The cron refresh becomes incremental: it recomputes only the hours and days that received readings since the previous run (watermark on inserted_at with 5 min overlap), so late batches of any age are aggregated. This replaces the fixed 48 h window and removes the gap with the 7 days ingest accepts. Migration 20261009100000.

title: ESP32 suspected of knocking out the home WiFi
description:
On 2026-10-08 the bench board ran from 17:02 to 22:03 (Madrid time). From 20:15 it had repeated internet outages of up to 17 minutes (DNS Failed, start_ssl_client -1). Around 21:00 the whole home network failed (the projector stopped working) and recovered as soon as the board was unplugged. The user is sure the board caused it.

There are documented cases of an ESP32 taking down a router: https://esp32.com/viewtopic.php?p=44018. Espressif put it down to an incompatibility between its WiFi driver and that router's firmware.

Measures:
1. WiFi.setSleep(false) in wifi_connection.cpp. Done; pending flash.
2. Search for known problems with the user's router model (model still unknown).
3. If it happens again: move to Arduino-ESP32 3.x (IDF 5, newer WiFi driver), and save logs with pio device monitor -f log2file plus a timestamped ping.
notes: Router: Sagemcom F@st 5366S, ISP Pepephone. Searches on 2026-10-09 found no documented case of an ESP32 knocking out this model. There are general complaints that the Pepephone Sagemcom routers drop the connection and need reboots, and a forum comment says ISP routers have little memory and lock up with many devices. Neither is confirmed for our case.

title: API: cached read endpoints on Vercel (/api/now, /api/day, /api/month, /api/daily)
description: Read layer between the browser and Supabase. Vercel api/ routes in the frontend project read Supabase with the secret key (Vercel env vars only, never in client code). Fixed endpoints, no free queries: /api/now (latest), /api/day?date=YYYY-MM-DD, /api/month?month=YYYY-MM, /api/daily (all days since install, ~365 rows/year). Cache-Control s-maxage: 60 s for now/today/current month; long (hours/days) for closed days/months since the past never changes. Strict param validation (format, no unknown params, no future dates, none before install) and 400 otherwise, so bots cannot bust the cache with random query strings. Device chosen by env var (bench vs station). Optional later: Vercel firewall rate limit per IP (check what the free plan includes).

title: Firmware: sensor self-check (boot + 's' on serial)
description: Print per-sensor status at boot and on demand: BME280 range, vane ADC disconnected threshold, reed pins idle HIGH + counts since boot, WiFi RSSI, time. Rules in a pure lib with native tests.

title: Backend: Supabase migrations + ingest Edge Function
description: readings, hourly, daily tables, RLS, pg_cron aggregates, ingest function with validation. Decide public vs restricted read.
notes: Decisions 2026-10-08 (revised): one Supabase project (no dev/prod split). No login for readers. Tables have NO select policy for anon: the publishable/anon key reads nothing. Reads go only through the Vercel API layer (meteo-b2c) using the Supabase secret key server-side. Scope here: readings, readings_hourly, readings_daily, pg_cron aggregates, RLS, ingest Edge Function (x-device-key). No read RPCs. Bench vs station separated by device_id (meteo-station-bench vs meteo-station-1). Deploy straight to remote (no local supabase start). Folder: backend/.

title: Phantom rain tip on the bench
description: On 2026-10-08 at 20:01 UTC the bench station counted one rain tip (0.2794 mm) with nobody touching the gauge. The network was failing at the time and the Mac may have gone to sleep or woken up. Possible causes: the bucket settling from near its balance point, or electrical noise on GPIO 33. Watch for more tips. If they repeat, look at the wiring and noise filtering on GPIO 33 before the station goes outside.
notes: The 2026-10-08 data shows 7 tips with nobody touching the gauge (Madrid time): 17:56, 20:15, 20:19, 20:24 (two), 20:35 and 22:01. Five fall at the start of the network outages. Hypothesis, unconfirmed: current spikes from the WiFi retries put noise on GPIO 33.
